If we are also querying 
`xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System` (line 724) then the result is not necessarily in the systems collection, right?

I thought systems collection only contains objects which have 
`"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.ManagedHost` interface.

> I thought systems collection only contains objects which have
"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.ManagedHost interface.

Yeah you are right, currently the multi-host collection only contains objects that specify `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.ManagedHost`. I removed the other interface. 

But following the PDI definition for `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System` we might as well update the collection handler to include the interface. I see other functions added to systems_utils, that also specify it.

nit: Just say "Managers"

managers.hpp is an implementation detail that we can see from your patch.  Manager is the API facing thing.

I don't think it's "all" right, it should be only the hosts that are managed by this bmc?

Just for clarification: ComputerSystem resources not managed by this BMC, are ComputerSystem resources aggregated from satellite bmcs?

In the multi-host case, this is every ComputerSystem in the collection, because they all implement the ManagedHost interface. 

But technically you are right. I have rephrased the commit message. Done
Please see the redfish checklist and execute it.
Not sure what you are exactly referring to.. I performed the testing for this patch similar to my other patches.

Since this comment thread has been stuck for over a month, here's my 2 cent


> Your change should not introduce any new validator errors. Please include
something to the effect of "Redfish service validator passing" in your commit
message.

Maybe the tested statements should be split and more explicit. Something like


```
Tested (RF Checklist 1.): documentation in Redfish.md up to date as per this schema
Tested (RF Checklist 2.): client facing change: in case multi-host option has been
           enabled, resource X now contains additional items ...
Tested (RF Checklist 3.): properties confirmed exist in CDSL schema
Tested (RF Checklist 4.): properties used for infrastructure management
Tested (RF Checklist 5.): RF service validator: no new errors
Tested (RF Checklist 6.): no new unit tests, external dependency on D-Bus
Tested (RF Checklist 7.): checked patch against COMMON_ERRORS.md
Tested (RF Checklist 8.): no new D-Bus interfaces introduced
```

I realize it's somewhat verbose but perhaps this could help reviewers pinpoint issues with the testing more easily since there's separate points to raise a comment on.
I have added a comment on the new behavior for ManagerForChassis on multi-host.
In support of this.
What's the holdup just using the new version of this code in all cases?

Currently no single-host implements the ManagedHost interface. I could however (and would rather like to) change the interface to xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System, which at least some single-hosts configure looking at EM upstream configs.

But even then, I expect to have name mismatches between BMCWEB_REDFISH_SYSTEM_URI_NAME and what is used for the dbus object representing the computer system on at least a few platforms. In these cases the validator will fail which should be considered a regression?

Closing this for now. As explained, this version regresses every single-host. However, as i am preparing a new thread on merging single- and multi-host code paths, correct handling should be discussed there.
This looks like it's assuming that every path hosted on the BMC is managed by the BMC.  I guess that's true for the ManagedHost interface?  Otherwise it would just be the host interface?

Yes, that is true for the ManagedHost interface.

>  Otherwise it would just be the host interface?

Just for clarification, do you mean `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System`?
I guess so, if it implies that the computer system implementing it, is also managed by the bmc. Looking at the description in PDI, that is not clear to me. (In that case I suggest to update the description)

Also could we do the same assumption for `ManagerForChassis`? Meaning, everything that implements Item.Chassis, can be considered to be managed by this BMC? Otherwise I would continue investigating towards associations

Using `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System` now, since this interface is used by both single- and multi-host platforms, unlike ManagedHost among other reasons I detailed in this patch [1].

> Otherwise it would just be the host interface?



Assuming you mean Item.System, yes that is my current understanding.


Marking this as resolved, unresolve if you feel like I am wrong about this.

[1] https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87160/1
